A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VINCIE, with matching authors, research objectives, data pipeline and benchmarks. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original MagicBrush and MSE-Bench experiments, ablations, human evaluations, metric correlations and qualitative generation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds expanded benchmark comparisons, annotation-quality evaluation, attention and camera-control ablations, and human evaluation of story generation.

M1.justification: V1 presents block-causal attention as the model architecture; v2 makes full attention the primary implementation and retains block-causal attention as a variant (Sections 1 and 3.2). V2 also introduces camera-token conditioning during training and static-camera prompting during inference (Appendix D.4), materially changing the described procedure.

E1.justification: V1 reports OmniEdit-based fine-tuning; v2 expands the reported training coverage to subject-driven, inpainting and in-context editing/generation data through X2I-subject-driven, X2I2 and SEED-X datasets (Appendix C.7). V2 additionally evaluates the LCT story-keyframe benchmark and demonstrates reference-guided background, color and expression transfer in Figure 20.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add evaluated comparators including Instruct-Pix2Pix, MagicBrush, ICEdit, OmniGen2, Step1X-Edit, Bagel, FLUX.1-Kontext, Qwen-Image-Edit and Nano Banana. V2 also adds In-context LoRA for story generation and replaces HQEdit, UltraEdit and OmniGen rows in the corresponding qualitative comparisons with newer baselines.

E3.justification: V1's MSE-Bench evaluation prompt requires binary judgments and termination after failure; v2's prompt evaluates the current turn using separate 0–10 prompt-following and consistency scores (Appendix C.6). This is a substantive reported protocol revision, although conversion to the tabulated success rates is unspecified. V2 also introduces a 500-instance annotation audit and human win/fail/tie evaluation for story generation.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing segmentation ablation with MagicBrush consistency measurements, while retaining the earlier MSE-Bench entries after rounding. New analyses examine annotation accuracy and recall, camera prompting, and RoPE/attention choices (Tables 8–10). Additional case studies test uncommon video-domain edits and fine-grained displacement control (Figures 14 and 25).

E5.justification: Table 7 retains the same correlation statistics and p-values. V2 does not introduce repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals or other uncertainty-estimation procedures; the new studies report point estimates.

E6.justification: Numerous entries change or are added. For example, Table 1's 7B+SFT turn-3 DINO changes from 0.739 to 0.775; Table 2 replaces the single 'Ours' row ending at 0.250 with several configurations, including 7B+SFT ending at 0.487. Changed training and grading prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. New results include annotation accuracy/recall of 75.14%/69.06% and story-generation preference results.

T1.justification: The likelihood factorization and context-dropout formulations in Equations 1–2 are retained. V2 adds architectural explanations and empirical analyses, but no new or substantively revised mathematical derivations, assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 removes block-causal architecture as a defining contribution from the abstract and conclusion, and presents full attention with an additional causal variant in the introduction. The central claims about learning from videos, scalability, MSE-Bench and emerging editing/generation capabilities remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of attention/RoPE tradeoffs, annotation noise versus scalability, camera/object-motion entanglement, and transfer of style/material knowledge from T2I/T2V foundation pretraining. It also distinguishes zero-shot composition from further fine-tuned reference editing and acknowledges limited story-generation evaluation. The original T5 and annotation-cost limitations are relocated, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: V2 supplies SFT dataset splits and access links, explains RGB replication and VAE encoding of segmentation masks, diagrams attention masks, and enumerates seven context compositions. It also discloses T2I alongside T2V foundation pretraining. Conversely, v1's explicit learning rate of 1e-4 disappears, leaving a reproducibility detail unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds references such as Magic Fixup, In-context LoRA, newer editing systems, and work on personalization, retrieval and post-training. These update the literature coverage, while the central positioning against synthesized pairwise editing data and the video-only learning novelty claim remain. The general image-editing review moves to Appendix B.

P1.justification: The main narrative and much of the wording are retained, with localized rewrites of architecture and application explanations. V2 reorganizes the appendices, moves general related work and limitations there, relabels broader impact as an ethics statement, and adds LLM-use and reproducibility statements.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the architecture figure, adds attention and context-composition diagrams, expands the main comparison tables, and restructures the segmentation table to include MagicBrush metrics. It also adds analysis tables and application figures, replaces baseline rows in qualitative grids, and changes figure placement and conference formatting. These exceed numerical updates or renumbering alone.

improvement.justification: Broader baselines, annotation auditing and targeted ablations strengthen v2's evidence. However, its new 0–10 grading prompt is not reconciled with the reported success rates or retained human-correlation validation. Section 4.3 also retains v1's 25% result and below-2% baseline discussion despite the revised Table 2. These inconsistencies affect central empirical conclusions, preventing a reliable judgment that the added evidence outweighs the loss of reporting clarity.
